chunks: 2532 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

“Whoever resides in Medina while intending hajj (pilgrimage) for a month or about that, then it occurs to him to depart by a route other than the road of Medina, then when he is opposite al-Shajarah and al-Bayda', at a distance of six miles, he should enter ihram from there.”

key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: al-Shajarah, the known miqat location near Medina
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءِ: al-Bayda', a location used here to identify the relevant point
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Medina, the city from which the pilgrim is residing or departing
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَمْيَالٍ: six miles, the measured distance mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.طَرِيقِ: route or road taken for departure
key_terms.فَلْيُحْرِمْ: he should enter ihram, indicating the legal instruction

ai.seo_question: Where should a person staying in Medina enter ihram if they leave for hajj by a route other than the usual road of Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the place of entering ihram for someone staying in Medina with the intention of hajj (pilgrimage), who later leaves by a different route. It specifies that when such a person reaches the point opposite al-Shajarah and al-Bayda', at six miles' distance, they should assume ihram there.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2532 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"Whoever resides in Medina intending to perform Hajj for a month or so, and then decides to depart on a route other than that of Medina, when they are opposite Al-Shajarah and Al-Bayda, a distance of six miles, they should assume Ihram from there."
